Ebiasaph
e-BYE-a-saf
n. (proper, a Levite of the sons of Korah; Hebrew, the father has gathered)
Hebrew Ebyacaph, from ab, father, and acaph, to gather — my father has gathered, or has added. He is a descendant of Korah, and his line kept the gates of the tabernacle.

Biblical Definition

He stands in the Kohathite pedigree: “Elkanah his son, and Ebiasaph his son, and Assir his son” (1 Chronicles 6:23), and again reckoned upward: “The son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah” (1 Chronicles 6:37). The office of his line is stated plainly: “And Shallum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brethren, of the house of his father, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the gates of the tabernacle” (1 Chronicles 9:19). Korah was the Levite who rose against Moses and Aaron and went down alive into the pit; and Numbers 26:11 records, in one of the most consequential asides in the Pentateuch, that the children of Korah died not. From that spared line came the doorkeepers of the tabernacle and the sons of Korah whose name stands over eleven psalms.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as a descendant of Korah, whose house were keepers of the gates of the tabernacle.

KORAHITE, n. A descendant of Korah the Levite; a family of doorkeepers and singers in the house of God.

DOORKEEPER, n. One who guards the entrance of a house or apartment; a porter.

REBELLION, n. An open and avowed renunciation of the authority of the government to which one owes obedience.

MERCY, n. That benevolence, mildness or tenderness of heart which disposes a person to overlook injuries.

PSALM, n. A sacred song or hymn; a composition consisting in praise or celebration of God.

Key Scripture

1 Chronicles 6:23 — "Elkanah his son, and Ebiasaph his son, and Assir his son,"

1 Chronicles 6:37 — "The son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah,"

1 Chronicles 9:19 — "And Shallum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brethren, of the house of his father, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the gates of the tabernacle: and their fathers, being over the host of the LORD, were keepers of the entry."

Numbers 26:11 — "Notwithstanding the children of Korah died not."

Modern Corruption

A family is assumed to inherit the reputation of its worst member, and Numbers 26:11 stands against it — the children of Korah died not, and their descendants kept God's doors and wrote his psalms.

expand to see more

Korah's rebellion is the most spectacular judgment in Numbers: the earth opened and swallowed him and his company, and fire consumed the two hundred and fifty. If ever a family name was ruined, that one was. And then, at the end of a genealogy where hardly anyone looks, Moses writes four words that change everything for that house: Notwithstanding the children of Korah died not. The judgment was exact. It fell where it was deserved and stopped where it was not, and Scripture takes the trouble to say so.

What God did with the spared line is the second half. Ebiasaph's descendants became keepers of the gates of the tabernacle — the sons of the man who had grasped at the priesthood were given the doors to guard — and eleven psalms are inscribed to the sons of Korah, including How amiable are thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts and As the hart panteth after the water brooks. The family that tried to seize the sanctuary was given a place in it by mercy, and its children sang some of the most tender lines in the Psalter.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Ebyacaph (H43), my father has gathered; acaph (H622), to gather; Qorach (H7141), Korah, bald; shaar (H8179), a gate.

expand to see more

Hebrew Ebyacaph (H43) — Ebiasaph; my father has gathered or added.

Hebrew acaph (H622) — to gather, to collect; the root also behind Asaph.

Hebrew Qorach (H7141) — Korah; the Levite who rose against Moses and Aaron.

Hebrew shaar (H8179) — a gate; the charge given to the Korahites.

Hebrew bene Qorach — the sons of Korah; the inscription over eleven psalms.

Usage

"“The son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah”."

"“Keepers of the gates of the tabernacle” — the office of the line."

"“Notwithstanding the children of Korah died not” — four decisive words."
